headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Notion AI can access workspace pages while langchain4j has no documented isolation or I/O surfaces, but direct prompt-injection and capability-conflict pathways are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented I/O surfaces or shared channel, while B can read workspace pages and is RAG-style over workspace content. That makes prompt injection plausible only if A’s content is manually copied into Notion or otherwise placed in a page B reads. The pairwise pathway is indirect and not default.
conditions: IF A-generated text is pasted into a Notion page that B later reads, injection becomes possible.
IF the operator creates a shared workspace channel between A and B, B may ingest attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of Notion pages unless reviewed.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions before pasting into B.
Mark imported content as untrusted in the workspace.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to pages consumed by B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B has shared workspace access and can read pages/databases the user can access, while A is an open-source LangChain4j component with no documented filesystem isolation or data-handling limits beyond network_egress none. If A processes sensitive workspace text before it is placed into B, or if B ingests sensitive pages, the pair can expose workspace content across the workflow. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF sensitive content is stored in pages accessible to B, B can surface it in outputs.
IF A is used to transform or summarize sensitive text before it is copied into Notion, that content can propagate into B.
mitigations: Restrict B to a non-sensitive workspace subset.
Avoid pasting secrets or regulated data into pages B can read.
Review A outputs before moving them into Notion.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and general content.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class tagging and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes no write or execution capabilities, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The only overlap is B’s shared workspace state, which does not create a direct write-write conflict with A. Because no shared mutable OS resource is documented, conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives A filesystem or git write access, conflict risk increases.
IF B is connected to a shared mutable resource outside Notion, concurrent edits may collide.
mitigations: Keep A read-only in the workflow.
Do not connect both agents to the same git repo.
Use one writer per workspace object.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a workspace Q&A and writing assistant grounded in content, so A’s outputs can become B’s inputs if copied into pages or databases. B does not show a built-in verification step, and A can generate unverified text. That creates a plausible cascade where A’s mistakes are rendered or acted on by B, though no direct autonomous action authority is documented.
conditions: IF A-generated summaries are inserted into pages that B uses as source material, B may amplify errors.
IF B is asked to draft decisions from A output without human review, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before ingestion.
Separate source notes from generated summaries in Notion.
Add a verification checklist before B drafts final text.
Label A outputs as untrusted drafts.
requires-engineering: add citation/grounding checks in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: B is vendor-hosted, uses Notion workspace permissions, and sends data to vendor backends/downstream model providers; A is docs-only open-source with no residency or retention controls documented. If regulated content is placed into B’s workspace, compliance depends on Notion’s policies rather than A’s controls. The pair therefore creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch, but not a proven breach.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated records are stored in pages B can access, residency/retention obligations may apply.
IF the operator relies on A for compliance handling, no such controls are documented.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B-accessible pages.
Confirm Notion’s DPA and retention settings before use.
Use a separate compliant workspace for regulated content.
Review workspace sharing permissions.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
